page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a local 959 GB SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a single-core stress-ng score of 1102.28 and a multi-core score of 2922.29, both categorized in the bottom 25 percent. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 163.34 GB/sec, but this drops to 19.71 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, which is in the bottom 10 percent. Computational benchmarks like Geekbench yield a single-core score of 934.0 and a multi-core score of 2030.0. Database operations and static web serving throughput are also limited, with Passmark database operations scoring 1083.99 and web serving throughput reaching 2.4 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.i2.xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and a substantial local SSD storage capacity, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring local data caching or moderate memory footprints without demanding high CPU throughput. However, the tradeoff is its weak processing and memory bandwidth performance. This instance is best suited for legacy database hosting, memory-bound applications with low CPU utilization, local file caching, and lightweight general-purpose workloads that benefit from dedicated vCPUs and local SSD storage rather than raw computational speed.
